summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain localized to her gastrostomy tube site, radiating to the left flank, with nausea and vomiting. She has a complex history including prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and reversal, post-surgical hypoglycemia, and gastrogastric anastomotic ulcers. Management was conservative: she was kept NPO initially, given IV fluids, and her G-tube was vented. Nausea was controlled with ondansetron and compazine, and pain was managed with acetaminophen and limited oxycodone. She gradually advanced to full liquids and tolerated oral intake well, with nutritional intake exceeding 75% of goal. A CT scan showed no acute intra-abdominal process, leak, or obstruction. Her blood glucose remained stable throughout. She was discharged home with instructions to continue PPI, sucralfate, Marinol, and ondansetron as needed, focus on small frequent meals, wear her Dexcom glucose monitor, and follow up with her dietitian and surgeon.
